title: Blocking vs non-blocking assignments: the one rule and why it exists
summary: Use <= in clocked blocks and = in combinational blocks. A shift register that collapses when written with = shows how the simulator's scheduler makes this rule necessary.

title: Binary, one-hot or Gray: how state encoding changes area, speed and safety
summary: State encoding decides how many flops an FSM uses, how deep its next-state logic is and what happens after an upset. Compare binary, one-hot and Gray, and learn to recover from illegal states.

title: Audio features for edge AI: from samples to a spectrogram
summary: Why small audio models are fed spectrograms rather than raw samples, and how to compute one step by step - framing, windowing, the FFT, mel scaling and the logarithm - with numpy code you can run.

title: Associativity, replacement and write policies: cache design choices compared
summary: Set associativity removes conflict misses, replacement picks a victim, and the write policy decides when memory is updated. Compare each choice with its hardware cost, including a pseudo-LRU tree worked by hand.

title: Array, Booth and Wallace: how hardware multipliers trade area for speed
summary: A multiplier generates partial products, reduces them to two rows and adds those. Compare array reduction, radix-4 Booth recoding and carry-save Wallace and Dadda trees, and where each spends area and delay.

title: Architecture of a smart energy meter SoC: core, metering engine, security and communications
summary: Why a smart meter SoC splits its work between a fixed-function metering engine, a small processor core, secure storage and communication interfaces, with a worked energy calculation and the reasoning behind each block.

title: Analog layout for matching: common centroid, interdigitation and dummies
summary: Process parameters drift across a die, so two identical transistors placed side by side are not identical. See how interdigitated and common-centroid patterns cancel gradients, and why dummies and orientation matter.

title: Amdahl's law for SoC designers: when an accelerator is worth it
summary: Speeding up one part of a workload helps only as much as the rest allows. Use Amdahl's law with data-movement overhead to decide, from a profile, whether a hardware accelerator earns its silicon.

title: Agile for hardware teams: what works when you cannot ship every week
summary: Which agile habits carry over to hardware and chip projects, where boards take weeks to arrive: short planning cycles, visible work boards, demos of intermediate results and fixed gates for irreversible steps.

title: Adding a custom instruction to a RISC-V core: when it beats a peripheral
summary: RISC-V reserves opcode space for your own instructions. Compare a custom instruction with a memory-mapped accelerator on overhead, datapath changes, toolchain and verification, and pick by the size of the work.

title: Accumulator width in quantized inference: avoiding overflow
summary: How many int8 products a 32-bit accumulator can safely sum, how to bound the real requirement per layer from its weights, why wrapping beats saturating mid-sum, and what hardware does when the bits run out.

title: AXI's five channels and why reads and writes are separate
summary: Why AXI splits a transaction into five handshaked channels, what the valid/ready rules prevent, how bursts and wrap addresses work, and how many outstanding transactions it takes to hide memory latency.

title: APB, AHB and AXI compared: picking a bus for each peripheral
summary: APB for simple registers, AHB for pipelined memory traffic, AXI for independent read and write streams. Work out each bus's bandwidth, match it to real peripherals, and write a small APB register block.

title: ADC datasheet terms decoded: ENOB, INL, DNL and SNR
summary: An ADC's bit count says little on its own. Learn what SNR, SINAD, ENOB, THD, SFDR, DNL and INL each measure, how they relate, and which ones matter for audio, sensing or control.

title: A risk register that people actually use
summary: How to write risks as cause, event and effect, rate them on probability and impact, give each an owner and a trigger, and review the register weekly so it changes decisions instead of gathering dust.

title: A resume for core electronics roles: projects over adjectives
summary: For chip and firmware roles, a resume works when it lists what you built, the tools you used and the result you checked. How to write project lines that hold up in an interview, on one honest page.

title: A power budget for a battery-powered rural IoT node
summary: Work out the battery life of a field sensor node from the charge each part uses per reporting cycle, see why the radio dominates, and test how weak coverage, retries and reporting rate change the answer.

title: A keyword-spotting pipeline from microphone to decision
summary: How an always-listening device turns a microphone stream into a yes or no - framing audio, computing features incrementally, running a small convolutional network on a sliding window, and smoothing decisions over time.

title: A PCB design review checklist for first boards
summary: A practical checklist for reviewing a first circuit board before you order it, covering power, decoupling, clocks, reset and boot, debug access, connectors and assembly, with the reason behind each check.
